impossibility_argument: Only C-level VALUES resist the admitted caller (tuple items, int attributes).
Custody is an owner->material MAPPING, so it must live in a container.

Every Python-level container the owner can reach is also caller-reachable and re-assignable: closure cell cell_contents, module global, class attribute, instance attribute (object.__setattr__ succeeds even on frozen dataclasses and __slots__), function __defaults__, function __code__, property, and WeakKeyDictionary (attacker-controlled __eq__/__hash__).
Therefore any secret the owner holds is READABLE by the caller.
Any value derived from it, including semantic_hash which is public, is RECOMPUTABLE.
Hence no custody binding built from Python-visible state can be non-forgeable against the admitted model.
Anchoring N independent containers only raises the attack from 1 primitive to N coordinated primitives; it does not establish non-forgeability.
one_line: The exact HQ234 04G attack is reproduced and now refused, and custody is genuinely anchored to the resolver's live containers with decision-time re-derivation, so every single admitted reflection primitive is closed. But a caller who substitutes all live anchors and rebinds the ledger in one coordinated step still mints custody, because no Python-visible anchor is unforgeable. The commission's required invariant is therefore NOT establishable inside the current pure-Python owner boundary.
productive_adequacy: all five lawful positive paths preserved; fail-closed correctness was not accepted as sufficiency

alternatives: process isolation: run the P07 owner in a separate process and hold custody behind a narrow IPC surface
OS-backed opaque handle: sealed file descriptor or keychain-backed token held opaquely by the owner
accept the residual risk explicitly and downgrade the F7 custody claim to 'adversarial-single-primitive'
smallest_architecture_change_required.cheapest_acceptable_if_native_is_deferre: the third alternative: state the residual coordinated-substitution risk as a known, accepted limitation rather than claiming non-forgeability
smallest_architecture_change_required.mechanism: a native opaque capability handle created once per resolver, holding the custody material in C memory with no Python-visible accessor, and exposing only 'is this handle the one sealed for resolver X' plus a resolve operation. The caller can then rebind every Python-level object and still cannot read, replace or forge the handle.
smallest_architecture_change_required.recommended: move the P07 owner custody ledger behind a small native (C-extension) boundary
